method: Market model event study. Alpha and beta are fitted by OLS on the 250 sessions ending 21 before each announcement; abnormal return is the stock's return minus what that fitted market sensitivity predicts. Window figures are buy-and-hold abnormal returns — compounded, the way a holder experiences them — while the event-time chart shows the cumulative daily path. Day 0 is the announcement session, which is mostly gapped and therefore mostly unbuyable; every other window starts at the day-0 close, the first price a retail account could actually pay. Deals with under 60 estimation observations fall back to a plain market adjustment and are labelled.
limits: Read the sample sizes before the medians. Fifteen events across five structures is not a dataset, it is a set of anecdotes with error bars, and the bootstrap intervals and sign-test p-values are printed so that is visible rather than hidden. The registry is also curated, which means selection bias: deals that made headlines are over-represented against quiet ones. Nothing here is a backtest, none of it is advice, and the forward ledger below is the only part that will ever be genuinely out of sample.

events.name: The Elmet Group
events.structure: $450M committed — redeemable preferred plus warrants for up to 19.9% — funding tungsten and molybdenum capacity. Newest deal on the board.

events.name: Alcoa
events.structure: ~$174M of equity in the project vehicle for the Wagerup gallium refinery, with offtake attached. The stake is in the project, not the parent.

events.name: IBM
events.structure: $1B toward a 300mm quantum wafer foundry venture for a minority non-controlling stake. Reported at LOI stage.

events.name: Rigetti Computing
events.structure: Up to $100M for a minority non-controlling stake, announced 21 May 2026 and definitive 8 Sep 2026. The definitive agreement moved the stock roughly a quarter as much as the announcement did.

events.name: D-Wave Quantum
events.structure: $100M CHIPS award for a minority stake of roughly 1.9%, part of a nine-company, ~$2B quantum tranche.

events.name: GlobalFoundries
events.structure: Two CHIPS awards totalling roughly $675M — quantum foundry and silicon photonics — for about 1.8% combined.

events.name: USA Rare Earth
events.structure: Letter of intent for access to up to $1.6B with an equity stake plus warrants. Non-binding: the terms in the headline are not yet the terms of a contract.

events.name: L3Harris
events.structure: $1B convertible preferred in the Missile Solutions unit, auto-converting at its spin-off IPO, tied to multi-year solid rocket motor procurement. Conversion is subject to appropriations.

events.name: Cameco
events.structure: Listed read-through to the $80B Westinghouse AP1000 partnership. The government's warrants sit in Westinghouse, which is private — holders own the partner, not the instrument.

events.name: Trilogy Metals
events.structure: $35.6M for 10% of common plus 7.5% in penny warrants, tied to the Ambler Road access decision in Alaska. Pre-production, so the stake is the whole story.

events.name: Lithium Americas
events.structure: Penny warrants for 5% of the company plus 5% of the Thacker Pass JV, tied to restructuring the $2.23B DOE loan. No cash outlay by the government and no revenue commitment attached.

events.name: Intel
events.structure: 9.9% of common (433M shares) at $20.47, converting $8.9B of unpaid CHIPS and Secure Enclave money. Additional 5% warrant only if Intel sells majority control of Foundry. No board seat, no stated exit.

events.name: Nvidia
events.structure: 15% of China H20 revenue paid to the government for export licences, later 25% on H200. Value flows out of the company, not in. Both chip names fell on the report.

events.name: AMD
events.structure: 15% of China MI308 revenue to the government in exchange for export licences. Same structure as Nvidia: a levy presented as a partnership.

events.name: MP Materials
events.structure: $400M convertible preferred at $30.03 plus warrants, ~15% as-converted. The economics that matter are contractual: a 10-year $110/kg NdPr price floor and 100% magnet offtake from the 10X facility.

exposure.name: GD
exposure.thesis: Submarine industrial base funding, with the same capital-return constraint attached.

exposure.name: HII
exposure.thesis: Maritime Action Plan and the Navy overhaul. The buyback restrictions cut the other way.

exposure.name: AVAV
exposure.thesis: Largest listed pure-play in small UAS as procurement dollars concentrate.

exposure.name: KTOS
exposure.thesis: Drone tariffs and the Pentagon fly-off programmes point at it.

exposure.name: METC
exposure.thesis: Rare earth build-out attached to an existing coal cash flow.

exposure.name: BWXT
exposure.thesis: Naval reactors and microreactors — a direct line into the SMR programmes.

exposure.name: UUUU
exposure.thesis: Uranium plus a running rare-earth separation line — the profile the DoW has repeatedly funded.

exposure.name: PPTA
exposure.thesis: Antimony and gold at Stibnite. Antimony is on every stockpile list and has no US production.

exposure.name: NB
exposure.thesis: Niobium, scandium and titanium at Elk Creek, with an existing EXIM and DoD funding history.

exposure.name: CRML
exposure.thesis: Tanbreez in Greenland. Administration interest has been reported; nothing is signed.

exposure.name: OKLO
exposure.thesis: Named in DOE fast-track lists. Pre-revenue, so entirely a policy-narrative position.

exposure.name: LEU
exposure.thesis: Domestic HALEU enrichment, the bottleneck in every advanced-reactor timeline.
